item.title: Hong Kong creates building maintenance regulator to address Tai Po fire failings
item.description: A new group tasked with overseeing building maintenance has been established to replace the Housing Bureau’s disgraced Independent Checking Unit, which was deemed culpable for a litany of failings leading up to last year’s Tai Po fire. item.title: Turkish authorities search for lioness spotted on Istanbul’s outskirts
item.description: Police and animal welfare teams in Istanbul are searching for a lioness seen prowling the city’s outskirts, according to Turkish officials. A resident spotted the animal on Sunday evening in Uskumrukoy, an upmarket neighbourhood on the northern edge of Istanbul’s European side, surrounded by forests. item.title: ‘Nothing came through’: why Boeing failed to land firm orders during Trump’s Shenzhen trip
item.description: US President Donald Trump, a self-described “Boeing salesman”, left China last week without securing firm orders for the 200 aircraft pledged during his visit to Beijing in May. Instead, the White House highlighted a Boeing deal struck during the Philippine leg of his Asian tour. item.title: University of Hong Kong puts on hold China human rights course as law dean steps down
item.description: The University of Hong Kong (HKU) will put on hold a course on human rights in China for master’s and Juris Doctor students in the second semester of the 2026-27 academic year, after convenor Fu Hualing said he was stepping down as dean of the law school. In a reply to the South China Morning Post on Monday, Fu said he had decided to cancel the course for the semester, but would resume teaching it
